one_line: How the Roman Empire actually worked — the machinery of power, spectacle and punishment, and the people it ground through.
pillars: Spectacle and Control (the arena, the triumph, punishment as public theatre)
The Frontier (legions, garrisons, and the edge of the known world)
Power and Punishment (law, sentencing, slavery, who the state could destroy)
The Machinery (engineering, grain, roads, money, logistics of empire)
The People Underneath (soldiers, slaves, the condemned, the poor)
audience: People who want Roman history as a system rather than a list of emperors — one startling fact, then the mechanism that makes it make sense.
tone: Plain, unsentimental, specific. States what the sources say and lets it be disturbing on its own. Every script closes on a flat one-line reframe rather than a summary.
hook_templates: Why the {place} was never only about {object}.
Nobody tells you what Rome did to {object}.
{object} was not what you think it was.
